page: Microsoft Azure D96ls_v7 is an x86_64 server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running at 4.2 GHz. It features 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The memory configuration consists of 192.0 GB of RAM, yielding a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The processor includes a 480 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix operations. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance, though it is Premium Storage capable.

In benchmark evaluations, the D96ls_v7 demonstrates strong multi-core performance, achieving a PassMark CPU score of 104,787.21 and a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 95,440.36, both placing in the top tiers. Single-threaded performance is also notable, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2,224.0 and gzip compression throughput of 36.54 GB/sec. Cryptographic and vector processing capabilities are highlighted by a PassMark CPU extended instructions test score of 119,233.71. Memory bandwidth is robust, reaching 333.72 GB/sec for large-block read operations, though the overall PassMark memory score sits in the average tier.

The primary tradeoff of the D96ls_v7 is its low memory density relative to its high compute capacity, making it less applicable for memory-intensive databases or large-scale in-memory caching. However, this resource distribution offers high qualitative cost efficiency for compute-bound workloads, as users do not pay a premium for unneeded RAM. The instance is optimized for multi-threaded decompression, static web serving, software compilation, and medium-sized LLM inference prompt processing, where its AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets can be fully leveraged.
